notes:
Account background: Spectra Velocity Analytics is a programmatic-adtech platform that performs realtime auction-time reranking and personalization for ad selection. Primary constraint: sub-100ms auction deadlines; any p95 spike above target causes lost bids and measurable rev impact.

Key contacts: Priya Nair (Head of Eng), Theo Martins (Platform), Anika Shah (SRE), Jordan Meyers (AE).

What they want / requirements:
- Workload: high-volume reranking + per-request personalization + on-the-fly embedding similarity for contextual filtering.
- Targets: p95 latency <= 60ms end-to-end for short prompts; sustained throughput 800-1,200 req/s per region during peak.
- Cost sensitivity: target 3x reduction in per-call compute cost vs current managed endpoint; looking for batching/caching/quantization levers to achieve.
- Model prefs: open model variants with proven quant profiles; willing to test 4-bit and 8-bit quantized variants but must validate quality on reranking metrics (NDCG, CTR lift).
- Routing/fallback: need multi-region routing + fallbacks to smaller models during capacity spikes (automatic).
- Security/compliance: enterprise SOC2 required; SSO/SAML; audit logs + KMS key control; data residency in US for PII-derived features.

POC summary (Jan–Mar 2026):
- Jan 14: Intro call (ff_20260214_sva_intro). Agreed to 2-week smoke POC on hosted API with synthetic auction traces.
- Jan 20–Feb 2: Smoke POC ran; initial baseline (hosted, default model) p95 ~120ms for 1-token rerank workflow at 400 rps.
- Feb 10: Migrated trial to Redwood Dedicated trial pool (small). Started controlled batching experiments (dynamic batch sizes 1-16).
- Feb 18: Perf review (ff_20260301_perf_review) — observed wide variance: batching reduced compute cost but increased tail latency for some traces (batched timeouts seen on cold routes).
- Feb 20–Mar 01: SE-run benchmarking with 10k synthetic traces (mixed short/long prompts) and KV caching enabled for repeated templates. Tested 8-bit quant (acceptable quality) and early 4-bit quant (quality drop on reranking metric ~2.8% NDCG). Ticket SUP-3492 opened for kernel selection issue on 4-bit path.

Notes from calls / quotes: "Spikes kill auctions — we need consistent 95th percentile under 60ms or this won't work in production" — Priya Nair.
"We care as much about predictable unit cost as raw latency. If batching helps cost but kills predictability, it's a non-starter." — Theo Martins.

Technical asks for next iteration:
- Run a 48h perf sweep across three regions with real traffic mimic (RPS distribution, template reuse). Provide breakdown: token-level cost, batching efficiency, KV cache hit rates, cold-start P95, and P50 per model variant.
- Provide recommended batching policy configs (max-latency-aware batching thresholds) and example rate-limited queue settings.
- Provide quantization profile matrix (8-bit / 4-bit) with sample evals on their rerank prompts and A/B impact on business metric proxy.
- Clear instrumentation: per-request trace id mapping to model variant, batch id, region, and cost.

Procurement/security path:
- Security reviewing SOC2 + ISO artifacts; need encryption-at-rest details and KMS integration doc (drive:/Spectra/Redwood_POC_Pricing_v1.pdf).
- Procurement requested SOW draft and estimated committed monthly GPU-hours for Dedicated plan (hold until perf sweep results).

Risks and open items:
- Quantization: 4-bit lowered NDCG in early tests; need Redwood Optimize suggestions / kernel tweaks.
- Batching trade-offs: ideal batching reduced token cost 2.8x but increased worst-case tail latency during bursts. Need adaptive batching thresholds.
- KV cache invalidation: ad templates change frequently; need TTL + versioning recommendations.

Next steps (short):
- Redwood to schedule 48h extended perf run week of 2026-03-15 (SE: Miguel Alvarez).
- SE to deliver per-model quant matrix and suggested batching configs by 2026-03-12.
- Security to receive SOC2 artifact and KMS integration doc; scheduled call 2026-03-08.
- Procurement to prepare draft SOW after perf run, targeted 2026-04-01.
